"""The domain objects a scenario is built from.

Trimmed to the fields Release 1 actually uses. The spec's AthleteProfile, group
membership, and subgroups are deliberately absent: the confirmed design models
one group per scenario, the travel party on the road or the whole roster at home.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from datetime import datetime, timedelta

from .temporal import Interval

__all__ = ["AssumptionSet", "Event", "KickoffAnchor", "ProtectedSleepWindow", "Scenario"]

# Obligations are mandatory by default. Only a kind named here may be ignored
# when computing opportunity, because the spec forbids improving the metric by
# dropping an activity without an explicit rule. A whitelist of *mandatory*
# kinds had the opposite effect: an unlisted or misspelled kind silently
# vanished from the calculation instead of blocking sleep.
OPTIONAL_KINDS = frozenset({"optional", "free", "unstructured"})


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class AssumptionSet:
    """What the staff assumed, recorded so a comparison can be reproduced.

    ``pre_bed_minutes`` is the time needed after an obligation ends before sleep
    can begin (the wind-down buffer); ``morning_minutes`` is the time needed
    before an obligation starts. Both consume opportunity and neither is
    inferred.

    ``saturday_night_wake`` is a wall time such as ``"09:00"``. Sunday is a
    player off day, so no obligation ends Saturday night; this assumed wake time
    does, and reports must label it as an assumption.
    """

    sleep_target_hours: float
    pre_bed_minutes: int
    morning_minutes: int
    source: str
    saturday_night_wake: str | None = None

    @property
    def pre_bed(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.pre_bed_minutes)

    @property
    def morning(self) -> timedelta:
        return timedelta(minutes=self.morning_minutes)


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class KickoffAnchor:
    """An event placed by its offset from kickoff rather than by clock time.

    Offsets are elapsed time from the kickoff *instant*. Resolving through the
    instant, not the wall clock, is what keeps "kickoff - 24h" correct when the
    event happens at home and the game is played in another zone.
    """

    start: timedelta
    end: timedelta
    start_zone: str
    end_zone: str | None = None

    def resolve(self, kickoff: datetime) -> Interval:
        return Interval(
            kickoff + self.start,
            kickoff + self.end,
            start_zone=self.start_zone,
            end_zone=self.end_zone or self.start_zone,
        )


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class Event:
    """An obligation. ``movable`` marks what a candidate scenario may shift."""

    id: str
    kind: str
    title: str
    interval: Interval
    movable: bool = False
    location: str | None = None
    # Set when the event was placed from kickoff. ``interval`` is still the
    # resolved truth; the anchor records how it was derived.
    anchor: KickoffAnchor | None = None

    @property
    def mandatory(self) -> bool:
        return self.kind not in OPTIONAL_KINDS


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ProtectedSleepWindow:
    """A sleep *opportunity* staff entered or a rule proposed.

    It is never inferred from free time. ``kind`` records where the opportunity
    sits (hotel, home, flight, nap) because those are not interchangeable.
    """

    id: str
    label: str
    interval: Interval
    kind: str = "hotel"
    proposed: bool = False
    # For a rule-proposed window, what set each edge: "curfew",
    # "obligation:<event id>", "wake-up call", "assumed wake", "staff override".
    start_source: str | None = None
    end_source: str | None = None


@dataclass
class Scenario:
    """A named plan: obligations, entered sleep windows, and its assumptions."""

    id: str
    title: str
    display_zone: str
    events: list[Event] = field(default_factory=list)
    windows: list[ProtectedSleepWindow] = field(default_factory=list)
    assumptions: AssumptionSet | None = None

    def obligations(self) -> list[Event]:
        return [e for e in self.events if e.mandatory]

"""Per-night reporting and comparison of two game weekends.

The decision this answers: does moving Friday practice, meetings, or a
departure change sleep opportunity on any night, and did the candidate quietly
move something that is not a lever?
"""

from dataclasses import replace
from datetime import timedelta

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.temporal import LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import build_weekend, compare_weekends, evaluate_weekend
from synthetic import (
    ASSUMPTIONS,
    CHICAGO,
    DENVER,
    EARLY_KICKOFF,
    H,
    road_early_released_template,
    road_early_template,
)

M = timedelta(minutes=1)
MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW = {"fri-meeting": (-13 * H, -12 * H - 10 * M)}  # 22:00-22:50 MT


def build(kickoff=EARLY_KICKOFF, id="baseline", assumptions=ASSUMPTIONS, **kwargs):
    return build_weekend(
        road_early_template(),
        kickoff,
        home_zone=CHICAGO,
        game_zone=DENVER,
        assumptions=assumptions,
        id=id,
        title=f"{id} (synthetic)",
        **kwargs,
    )


def candidate(**kwargs):
    return build(id="candidate", **kwargs)


def test_each_night_of_the_weekend_is_reported_separately():
    report = evaluate_weekend(build())
    assert [n.night for n in report.nights] == ["thu", "fri", "sat"]
    # Thu 23:00-07:00 CT, Fri 23:00-06:00 MT, Sat 23:00 CT to assumed 09:00 CT.
    assert [n.hours for n in report.nights] == [8.0, 7.0, 10.0]


def test_night_reporting_interval_is_fixed_by_date_not_by_the_proposed_window():
    base = evaluate_weekend(build()).night("fri").report.reporting_interval
    late = evaluate_weekend(candidate(offsets=MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW)).night("fri").report.reporting_interval
    assert late == base
    assert (base.wall("start"), base.wall("end")) == ("2026-10-02T18:00", "2026-10-03T12:00")
    assert base.start_zone == DENVER


def test_meetings_running_past_curfew_compare_cleanly_and_show_the_loss():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(offsets=MEETINGS_PAST_CURFEW))
    assert comparison.night("fri").hours_delta == pytest.approx(-20 / 60, abs=1e-6)
    assert comparison.night("thu").hours_delta == 0.0
    assert comparison.night("sat").hours_delta == 0.0


def test_moving_friday_practice_earlier_changes_no_night_while_curfew_binds():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(offsets={"fri-practice": (-23 * H, -21 * H)}))
    assert [comparison.night(n).hours_delta for n in ("thu", "fri", "sat")] == [0.0, 0.0, 0.0]
    assert [c.event_id for c in comparison.changed_events] == ["fri-practice"]
    assert comparison.fixed_event_changes == []
    assert comparison.flags == []

    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(kickoff=LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:30", DENVER)))
    assert comparison.kickoff_shift == 30 * M
    assert comparison.changed_events == []


def test_kickoff_change_is_flagged_because_kickoff_is_not_a_lever():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(kickoff=LocalTime("2026-10-03T11:30", DENVER)))
    assert any("kickoff" in flag for flag in comparison.flags)


def test_candidate_that_moves_a_fixed_template_event_is_flagged():
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(offsets={"sat-meal": (-5 * H, -4 * H)}))
    assert [c.event_id for c in comparison.fixed_event_changes] == ["sat-meal"]
    assert any("sat-meal" in flag for flag in comparison.flags)


def test_late_return_costs_saturday_night_against_the_assumed_wake():
    # Return charter lands 04:00 CT instead of 20:00 CT: 10h becomes 4h30m.
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(), candidate(offsets={"sat-depart": (14 * H, 16 * H)}))
    assert comparison.night("sat").hours_delta == -5.5
    assert comparison.flags == []


def test_weekends_built_on_different_assumptions_are_refused():
    with pytest.raises(ValueError, match="assumption"):
        compare_weekends(build(), candidate(assumptions=replace(ASSUMPTIONS, pre_bed_minutes=60)))


def test_obligation_dropped_from_the_candidate_is_flagged():
    from sleep_scheduler.schedule import Event

    film = Event(

        kind="meeting",
        title="Thursday film",
        interval=Interval.of("2026-10-01T19:00", "2026-10-01T20:00", CHICAGO),
    )
    comparison = compare_weekends(build(extra_events=[film]), candidate())
    assert comparison.removed_events == ["thu-film"]
    assert any("thu-film" in flag and "missing" in flag for flag in comparison.flags)


def test_night_without_a_window_reports_zero_with_its_reason():
    night = evaluate_weekend(build(offsets={"fri-meeting": (-13 * H, -4 * H - 30 * M)})).night("fri")
    assert night.hours == 0.0

"""Compare two game-weekend files and print sleep opportunity night by night.

Usage::

    python -m sleep_scheduler fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-baseline.json \\
                              fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-candidate.json

The wording here is deliberately constrained. The report says "opportunity",
names the source of its target, labels every assumption as one, says what set
each edge of each sleep window, and prints the forecast status rather than a
forecast. It has no vocabulary for effectiveness, fatigue, or readiness,
because nothing in this codebase can compute them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from datetime import timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .adapter import get_adapter
from .persistence import load_weekend
from .weekend import NightReport, WeekendComparison, compare_weekends

__all__ = ["main", "render_weekend_comparison"]


def _hhmm(hours: float) -> str:
    total = round(abs(hours) * 60)
    return f"{total // 60}h {total % 60:02d}m"


def _signed_hhmm(hours: float) -> str:
    return ("+" if hours >= 0 else "-") + _hhmm(hours)


def _shift(delta: timedelta) -> str:
    minutes = round(delta.total_seconds() / 60)
    if minutes == 0:
        return "unchanged"
    direction = "later" if minutes > 0 else "earlier"
    return f"{abs(minutes) // 60}h {abs(minutes) % 60:02d}m {direction}"


def _window_line(label: str, night: NightReport) -> str:
    name = night.night.capitalize()
    window = night.plan.window
    if window is None:
        return f"  {label} {name}: no window ({night.note})"
    zone = ZoneInfo(window.interval.start_zone)
    start = window.interval.start.astimezone(zone).strftime("%a %H:%M")
    end = window.interval.end.astimezone(zone).strftime("%a %H:%M")
    return (
        f"  {label} {name}: {start} -> {end} {window.interval.start_zone} "
        f"(start: {window.start_source}; end: {window.end_source})"
    )


def render_weekend_comparison(comparison: WeekendComparison) -> str:
    baseline, candidate = comparison.baseline, comparison.candidate
    weekend = candidate.weekend
    assumptions = weekend.scenario.assumptions
    lines: list[str] = []

    lines.append("Measure: sleep opportunity (not sleep obtained), reported per night")
    lines.append(f"Baseline:  {baseline.weekend.scenario.title}")
    lines.append(f"Candidate: {weekend.scenario.title}")
    kickoff = weekend.kickoff.astimezone(ZoneInfo(weekend.game_zone))
    lines.append(
        f"Kickoff: {kickoff:%a %Y-%m-%d %H:%M} {weekend.game_zone} "
        f"({weekend.template.band} band); home zone {weekend.home_zone}"
    )
    lines.append(f"Template: {weekend.template.source}")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append(f"{'Night':<6}{'Baseline':>10}{'Candidate':>11}{'Difference':>12}")
    for name, night in comparison.nights:
        lines.append(
            f"{name.capitalize():<6}{_hhmm(night.baseline.hours):>10}"
            f"{_hhmm(night.candidate.hours):>11}{_signed_hhmm(night.hours_delta):>12}"
        )
    shortfalls = ", ".join(
        f"{name.capitalize()} {_hhmm(night.candidate.shortfall_hours)}"
        for name, night in comparison.nights
    )
    lines.append(f"Candidate shortfall against target: {shortfalls}")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append("Protected sleep windows (what set each edge):")
    for label, report in (("Baseline", baseline), ("Candidate", candidate)):
        for night in report.nights:
            lines.append(_window_line(label, night))
    lines.append("")

    lines.append(f"Target: {_hhmm(assumptions.sleep_target_hours)} (source: {assumptions.source})")
    lines.append(
        f"Assumptions: wind-down buffer of {assumptions.pre_bed_minutes} min after the last "
        f"obligation; {assumptions.morning_minutes} min before a morning obligation"
    )
    if assumptions.saturday_night_wake:
        lines.append(
            f"Saturday night ends at an assumed wake time of {assumptions.saturday_night_wake} "
            "(an assumption, not an obligation: Sunday is a player off day)"
        )
    lines.append("")

    if comparison.changed_events:
        lines.append("Changed events:")
        for change in comparison.changed_events:
            lines.append(
                f"  - {change.event_id}: start {_shift(change.shift)}, end {_shift(change.end_shift)}"
            )
    else:
        lines.append("Changed events: none")
    if comparison.added_events:
        lines.append(f"Added in candidate: {', '.join(comparison.added_events)}")

    if comparison.flags:
        lines.append("Flags:")
        for flag in comparison.flags:
            lines.append(f"  ! {flag}")
    else:
        lines.append("Flags: none (only movable events changed)")
    lines.append("")

    conflicts = [
        (label, night.night, conflict)
        for label, report in (("Baseline", baseline), ("Candidate", candidate))
        for night in report.nights
        for conflict in night.report.conflicts
    ]
    if conflicts:
        lines.append("Conflicts (not resolved automatically):")
        for label, name, conflict in conflicts:
            lines.append(f"  - {label} {name.capitalize()}: {conflict.describe()}")
    else:
        lines.append("Conflicts: none")
    lines.append("")

    adapter = get_adapter()
    first_night = candidate.nights[0].report
    result = adapter.simulate(first_night, requires_travel=weekend.home_zone != weekend.game_zone)
    lines.append(f"Forecast ({result.adapter_name} v{result.adapter_version}): {result.reason}")
    warnings: list[str] = []
    for night in candidate.nights:
        for warning in adapter.validate(night.report):
            if warning not in warnings:
                warnings.append(warning)
    for warning in warnings:
        lines.append(f"  ! {warning}")

    return "\n".join(lines)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="sleep_scheduler",
        description="Compare sleep opportunity night by night between two game-weekend files.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("baseline", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("candidate", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        comparison = compare_weekends(load_weekend(args.baseline), load_weekend(args.candidate))
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        print(f"error: cannot read {exc.filename}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    except (ValueError, KeyError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    print(render_weekend_comparison(comparison))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

- **Start** = curfew; or, on a night the itinerary gives no curfew (Saturday), the end of the releasing obligation (`released_by`: the bus back to the facility, or the game at home) plus the assumed release-to-bed time (`release_to_bed_minutes`). The start is then pushed past any obligation that **begins before it**, plus the wind-down buffer.
- **End** = the wake-up call from the template, resolved from kickoff or clock.
- **Saturday night**: Sunday is a player off day, so the end is the Saturday assumed wake time from the assumption set, and the report labels that bound as an assumption rather than an obligation.

An obligation that begins after the start does not move it: it stays inside the window as a reported conflict and costs only its own time (an overnight treatment; a breakfast window that opens before the wake-up call). Implemented 2026-09-16; before that any obligation starting before the end pushed the start, which erased a real Friday night.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

Release 1 design confirmed 2026-09-15 (decisions table in
`SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md`). Package 1 (calendar core) and Package 1b
(game-weekend model) are implemented test-first on branch
`worktree-calendar-core`, draft PR #1. 163 tests pass; run `python -m pytest`
from the repo root. Records: `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-game-weekend-model.md`
(model build, itinerary review).

**2026-09-16: the model was reshaped for the real itineraries.** The six
itinerary questions were adopted at their recommended answers as **working
assumptions pending staff confirmation**; see the table under "Working
assumptions" in the spec's "Protected sleep window rule" section. Built
test-first:

- **Clock-time anchoring.** `weekend.ClockTime(day, "HH:MM")` (day counted from
  game day, `-1` = Friday) can place a template entry's edges or a night's
  curfew/wake instead of a kickoff offset. An entry uses one anchoring for both
  edges. Clock entries carry no `KickoffAnchor`, so a kickoff change moves
  Saturday and reports nothing for Friday. Offset overrides must match the
  entry's anchoring.
- **Window start rule (closes old open question 7).** Only an obligation that
  begins before the current start pushes it. Later ones stay inside the window
  as reported conflicts. A breakfast window opening before the wake-up call now
  clips the night instead of erasing it.
- **Nights without a curfew.** `NightMarker(curfew=None, released_by=<event id>)`
  starts at that event's end + `AssumptionSet.release_to_bed_minutes`
  (source `release:<id>`). The CLI prints and labels that assumption.
- **File format.** Optional keys `<edge>_clock`, `released_by`,
  `release_to_bed_minutes`; `FORMAT_VERSION` still 1, old fixtures load
  unchanged, and the CLI example output is unchanged.

Checked in memory against the real Auburn times (nothing saved): Friday with
breakfast as check-in 21:30 → 08:45 ET, 11h15m, set by curfew, which matches the
Drive review. As a whole breakfast block it is 10h00m with a visible conflict,
where it was 0h before. Saturday: bus arrival 23:15 CT + 45m → 00:00, 9h to the
assumed 09:00 wake.

The first two real staff itineraries (Auburn, PVAMU) live on Drive, not in Git:
`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\99_UNSORTED\From_Desktop\TECHNOLOGY\FAST\GAME_WEEK_ITINERARIES\2026\`,
with extracted times and offsets in `extracted-timeline-review.md` there.

Working example — the Friday early-kickoff comparison:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m sleep_scheduler \
  fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-baseline.json fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-candidate.json
```

An early road kickoff: 11:00 MT Saturday, home in Central time. In the baseline
Friday meetings run 22:00–23:00 MT, so with a 30-minute wind-down the Friday
window starts at 23:30 instead of the 23:00 curfew: 6h30m. Moving meetings an
hour earlier lets curfew set the start: 7h00m, +30m. Thursday (8h) and Saturday
(10h, to an assumed 09:00 wake) are unchanged, and only a movable event changed,
so there are no flags. Every offset, curfew, and wake time is synthetic. This
fixture still uses offset anchoring and a Saturday curfew; the synthetic
`home_night_template()` in `tests/synthetic.py` shows the itinerary-shaped form
(clock Friday, breakfast check-in, released Saturday).

Modules, all under `src/sleep_scheduler/`:

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| `temporal.py` | Local wall time + IANA zone → UTC instant; half-open intervals; merge/subtract |
| `schedule.py` | Event (optional `KickoffAnchor`), ProtectedSleepWindow (edge sources), AssumptionSet (`saturday_night_wake`, `release_to_bed_minutes`), Scenario |
| `opportunity.py` | Spec steps 1–8; conflicts; comparison with changed, removed, added, and fixed-event changes |
| `weekend.py` | Kickoff bands, `ClockTime`, templates, `build_weekend`, the sleep window rule, `evaluate_weekend` / `compare_weekends`, flags |
| `adapter.py` | Forecast seam; the only adapter returns a status, never a number |
| `persistence.py` | Scenario JSON round-trip; game-weekend files (inputs only, rebuilt on load) |
| `cli.py` | `python -m sleep_scheduler <baseline weekend> <candidate weekend>` |

## Design confirmed (2026-09-15)

The full answer table is in `SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md` under "Release 1 design
decisions". In short: Release 1 compares Baylor football game weekends
(Thursday evening to Sunday midday) for **Friday practice/meeting times against
Saturday kickoff** and **road-game departures, including the late return**. It
reports sleep opportunity per night for one group (the travel party, or the
whole roster at home). Applied Performance runs it locally: CSV in, one-page
HTML comparison out. There is no Sunday lift (player off day), and subgroups
are out of Release 1.

## Next

1. **Staff confirm the six working assumptions** (spec table) and **verify the
   extracted itinerary times** in the Drive review file. Both are human steps.
   If an answer differs, the model already supports the alternative except
   decision 1–2 "no" (kickoff-anchored Friday), which is just offset entries.
2. **Draft real templates on Drive** (afternoon band from Auburn, night band
   from PVAMU) once times are verified: clock-time Friday, kickoff Saturday,
   breakfast as check-in, "available" items optional, Saturday
   `released_by` the bus/game, no Thursday marker, neutral site as road. Load
   from Drive; never commit.
3. **Package 2:** CSV template shaped like the staff itinerary (time, item,
   location, duration, zone marker on travel legs). It must express both
   anchorings and `released_by`.
4. **Package 3:** printable one-page HTML comparison; the CLI report is its
   content model.

- Deferred out of Release 1: forecast engine, subgroups/non-travel,
  `SleepObservation`, candidate generation (CP-SAT), archive migration, the
  athlete mobile itinerary, hosting and roles.
- `AGENTS.md` still carries an unfolded `.from-windows` merge block (a stale
  pre-interview copy); safe to delete once someone confirms nothing in it is
  wanted.

## Open questions

1. The six itinerary assumptions above: confirmation pending (staff).
2. A home game with a Friday hotel uses `at="away"` (game zone = home zone) to
   mark the Friday window as a hotel window. Fine for now; revisit if a
   template needs a hotel in the home zone on a road trip.
3. Should the first obligation after the start ever push it (a travel leg
   departing after curfew)? Under a curfew it is now a conflict. Real itineraries
   put no travel after curfew, and Saturday uses release instead. Revisit only
   if a real case appears.

Still needed from staff: verification of the extracted itinerary times, an
early-kickoff itinerary, and confirmation of the 30-minute wind-down buffer.

## Gotchas

- **Real itineraries never go in Git.** They are team schedules (AGENTS.md
  archive boundary). Keep them and anything derived from them on Drive. The
  synthetic home template copies their *shape*, never their times.
- `zoneinfo` does not refuse impossible local times; `temporal.LocalTime`
  raises on DST gaps and ambiguous times. Do not bypass it. `ClockTime`
  resolves through it.
- `Interval` equality ignores zone provenance on purpose; round-trip tests
  compare serialized dicts to check zones.
- Events are mandatory **by default**; only `schedule.OPTIONAL_KINDS` are
  ignored. Never reintroduce a mandatory whitelist. "Treatment available"-style
  items must be entered with an optional kind.
- Curfew and wake-up are `NightMarker`s, never Events. A marker has exactly one
  of `curfew` or `released_by`.
- The wind-down buffer **is** `pre_bed_minutes`; do not add a second field.
  `release_to_bed_minutes` is different: it *replaces* the buffer at a
  released night's start.
- `morning_minutes` widens the block before every obligation and can clip the
  window before a wake-up call; fixtures use 0.
- A staff end override is settled before obligations are checked; a start
  override is applied after.
- Night reporting intervals are fixed by date (18:00–12:00 in the night's zone,
  dated from the start before any push). Never derive them from the proposed
  window.
- Kickoff-anchored events compare by offset; a kickoff change is one
  `kickoff_shift`. Clock events compare by instant. Change detection covers
  start, end, removed, and added.
- `ClockTime.day` counts from the kickoff date **on the stadium clock**.
- Game-weekend files store inputs and are rebuilt on load; never add resolved
  instants. Newer keys are optional, so `FORMAT_VERSION` is 1.
- The CLI reads game-weekend files only; `--window` is gone.
- Itinerary "EST/CST" in September means daylight time; use IANA zones.
- The synthetic fixtures were generated once from `tests/synthetic.py`; the
  generator was not kept. Edit the JSON directly.
- On Windows, Python rewrites files with CRLF; `core.autocrlf=true` normalizes
  on commit. Bash heredocs containing large Python patch scripts failed to parse
  here; use the Edit tool.

# Memory Write

## Outcome
- Fact added to, updated in, or removed from the correct memory tier
- Tier-B caps enforced (2,500 chars for MEMORY.md, 1,375 for USER.md)
- Confirmation: "Saved — will be active from next session."

## Pick the tier first

Ask: "Will this fact still be true and useful in 3 months, across multiple projects?"

**Tier A — `~/.claude/projects/<slug>/memory/`** (one file per fact, indexed by MEMORY.md)
- Durable user facts → `user_*.md` (metadata.type: user)
- Stable project conventions / gotchas → `project_*.md` (metadata.type: project)
- Behavioral feedback rules → `feedback_*.md` (metadata.type: feedback)
- External-system pointers → `reference_*.md` (metadata.type: reference)

**Tier B — `~/.claude/global-memory/`** (single capped file)
- Active threads (in-progress work) → `MEMORY.md` `## Active Threads`
- Current env notes (URLs, tool versions, project structure in play) → `MEMORY.md` `## Environment Notes`
- Pending decisions → `MEMORY.md` `## Pending Decisions`
- Durable user profile updates → `USER.md`

## Steps

1. **Decide tier** using the rule above.
2. **Read** the target file in full.
3. **Dedup check** — substring scan; if the fact already exists, skip or update in place.
4. **Cap check** for Tier B — `wc -c < ~/.claude/global-memory/MEMORY.md` (or USER.md). If over cap, consolidate (merge similar entries, prune stale) before adding.
5. **Write** the change.
   - Tier A: create a new file with proper frontmatter (name, description, metadata.type) and add a one-line pointer to that slug's `MEMORY.md` index. `name:` follows the rule below.
   - Tier B: append under the correct `##` section.
6. **Confirm** in one line: `Saved — will be active from next session.`

## The `name:` field — bare kebab slug

**`name:` = the filename stem minus its leading type token, kebab-cased.** The type
already lives in `metadata.type` and the filename already carries the prefix; repeating
it in `name:` is the third copy.

| File | `name:` |
|---|---|
| `project_automation-cadence.md` | `automation-cadence` |
| `user_sports-teams.md` | `sports-teams` |

corpus split 59 bare / 58 prefixed, which broke 37 links. Both forms look right in

## Actions

- **add** — append (default)
- **replace** — substring match + swap. Preferred over add when updating an existing fact.
- **remove** — confirm with the user before deleting.

## Retrieval — the tiered ladder

When the user asks about past context, decisions, or "did we already…?", climb in order and stop as soon as the question is answered. Do not run memsearch when the answer is already in the injected snapshot.

1. **Tier 0** — scan what is already in context (USER.md, MEMORY.md, today's compiled log). Zero cost.
2. **L1** — `memsearch search "query" --top-k 5`. Hybrid vector + keyword across all indexed paths: Tier A files (including the Windows-machine slugs), daily logs, transcripts.
3. **L2** — `memsearch expand <chunk_hash>`. Full markdown section around a hit.
4. **L3** — `memsearch transcript <session_id>`. Raw dialogue. Last resort.
5. **Fallback** — say "I don't have a record of that."

## Daily compiled logs — read-only

`~/.claude/claude-memory-compiler/daily/{YYYY-MM-DD}.md` is produced by `claude-memory-compiler` through its own SessionEnd/PreCompact hooks, and injected by its own SessionStart hook.

- **Never hand-edit these files.** The compiler owns them.
- **Never read them eagerly.** Treat the injected snapshot as the source of truth.

## What is loaded at session start

`~/.claude/global-memory/USER.md` and `MEMORY.md` are read once at session start and are a **frozen snapshot**. Mid-session writes persist to disk but only take effect next session — this is deliberate, to preserve the prefix cache. Never load more than the startup set proactively.

## Rules

- Never exceed Tier B caps. Consolidate first.
- Always dedup before adding.
- For Tier A, the slug is the current cwd with `/` and `.` replaced by `-` (so `~` → `-Users-kristinarash`, `~/DEV` → `-Users-kristinarash-DEV`, `~/.claude/skills` → `-Users-kristinarash--claude-skills`). The harness injects the correct slug each session — use that, don't reconstruct it.
- **Write only to the current machine's slug.** Both machines are active as of 2026-09-10: Mac slugs are `-Users-kristinarash-*`, Windows slugs are `C--Users-eric-rash-*`. A fact written to the other machine's slug is never auto-injected here (memsearch still finds it). Durable project facts belong in the repo's `docs/` so both machines see them.
- Never announce the write mid-session beyond the one-line confirmation. The injected snapshot is frozen — the new fact appears next session, not this one.

## Verification Gate

After every write:

1. Read the exact destination back and require the intended fact to appear once in the intended tier.
2. Re-run the Tier B character cap check after the write.
3. Check the surrounding section for an unresolved contradiction or stale duplicate. Resolve it or report `FAIL`.
4. For Tier A, verify the new file has valid frontmatter and the memory index pointer resolves to it.
5. Distinguish persisted state from activation: the write can pass now, but next-session injection remains unverified until a later session observes it.

Report `PASS` only when persistence, uniqueness, tier placement, caps, and pointers are verified. Report `FAIL` with the target path and failed check otherwise. Do not emit “Saved” before read-back succeeds.

**What changed** (test-first, 133 → 163 tests):
- **Friday on the clock:** templates can now place an event, a curfew or a wake-up call at a local time on a given day ("Friday 21:30"), not only as an offset from kickoff. If kickoff moves, Saturday moves and Friday stays where staff put it, and the comparison doesn't report Friday events as moved.
- **When an obligation delays sleep:** an obligation only pushes the start of sleep if it begins before the current start, such as meetings running past curfew. One that begins later, like an overnight treatment or breakfast opening before the wake-up call, stays inside the night and is reported as a conflict. This closes the old open question about which obligations push the start.
- **Saturday without a curfew:** the night starts a set time after the event that releases players (the game, or the bus back to the facility). That time is a new, labelled assumption: 45 minutes for real templates, and the report prints it as an assumption.

- **Friday, breakfast entered as its check-in:** 11h15m, set by curfew, which matches the Drive review.

# Sleep Scheduler

A rebuild of the legacy FAST scheduling workflow for athlete sleep and team travel. The repository name is institution-neutral; the initial use case remains Baylor athletes and team travel.

## Current status

Research and static installer inspection are complete, and the Release 1 design was confirmed with the user on September 15, 2026 (see the decisions table in [the specification](SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md)). Release 1 compares Baylor football game weekends night by night: Friday practice and meeting times against Saturday's kickoff, and road-game departures including the late return.

Built so far: kickoff-anchored events, kickoff-band templates, the protected sleep window rule, per-night comparison with flags for anything fixed that changed, a game-weekend file format, and a command-line report over synthetic fixtures. **No forecasting engine has been selected, implemented, or validated.** See [docs/STATUS.md](docs/STATUS.md) for what is built and what is next.

```bash
python -m pytest
PYTHONPATH=src python -m sleep_scheduler \
  fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-baseline.json fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-candidate.json
```

The tool reports sleep *opportunity* only. It has no vocabulary for effectiveness, fatigue, or readiness, and the sole model adapter returns a status rather than a number. Every template offset, curfew, and wake time in `fixtures/` and `tests/` is synthetic, not Baylor's game-week timeline.

3	Status: Release 1 design confirmed with the user on September 15, 2026, through the design interview recorded below. Research basis: [FAST modernization research](FAST-MODERNIZATION-RESEARCH.md). No physiological model has been implemented or validated.
4	
5	## Product objective
6	
7	Help Applied Performance compare feasible Baylor football game-weekend schedules that protect sleep opportunities around practice, meetings, travel, and competition. Provide a reproducible explanation of each difference. Add fatigue predictions through an explicitly identified model only after its capabilities and evidence have been evaluated.
8	
9	The decisions Release 1 supports are:
10	
11	- **Friday practice and meeting times** relative to Saturday's kickoff.
12	- **Departure times** for road games, outbound and post-game (the late return).
13	
14	The first complete workflow is a Friday comparison before an early road kickoff: build a baseline game weekend from a kickoff-band template; duplicate it; move Friday practice or meeting times; compare per-night opportunity and conflicts; export a one-page comparison. Use synthetic data for development. Historical football schedules become fixtures only after staff verifies their interpretation.
15	
16	## Release 1 design decisions (interview, 2026-09-15)
17	
18	| # | Decision | Settled answer |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| Q1/Q16 | Decision the app improves | Friday practice/meeting timing against Saturday kickoff, and road-game departures including the late return. First working example: Friday times before an early road kickoff. |
21	| Q2 | Forecasting | Sleep opportunity only. An engine is expected later; not a FAST replacement until then. |
22	| Q3/Q12/Q19 | Who is modelled | One group per scenario: the travel party (road) or the full roster (home). No subgroups, no individual athlete data, no non-travel reporting in Release 1. |
23	| Q4 | Operation | Applied Performance creates and interprets; coaches and operations review the one-page comparison and decide. Athletes are not users. |
24	| Q5 | Scenario unit | One game weekend, Thursday evening through Sunday midday. Road games and home games with a Friday team hotel. Neutral-site games are road games (confirmed 2026-09-16). |
25	| Q6 | Kickoff anchoring | Game-related events are stored as offsets from kickoff; changing kickoff re-flows them. Comparing kickoff slots = duplicate and change kickoff. Amended 2026-09-16: Friday curfew, practice, and meetings are clock times chosen per week; kickoff drives Saturday. |
26	| Q7 | Movable levers | Departures, Friday practice, and meeting times. Kickoff is fixed. |
27	| Q10 | Sunday | Player off day. No lift on Sunday (lifts are Monday and Wednesday). |
28	| Q11 | Sleep window rule | Rule-proposed per night from explicit practice times, practice lead time before kickoff, curfew, and meeting times (see "Protected sleep window rule"). |
29	| Q13/Q18 | Templates | Same timeline shape each week, timing varies with kickoff: three kickoff-band templates. |
30	| Q14 | Target | One editable target for all nights. |
31	| Q17 | Saturday night | Ends at an editable assumed wake time, labelled as an assumption. |
32	| Q9 | Input and output | CSV template shaped like the operations itinerary in; printable one-page HTML comparison out. |
33	| Q15 | Deployment | Local on the Applied Performance laptop. No hosting, login, or roles. |
34	
35	Values still needed from staff (data, not decisions): real template offsets per band, the Saturday assumed wake time, and confirmation of the 30-minute wind-down default. Fixtures use visibly synthetic values until then.
36	
37	## Release 1 scope
38	
39	Input is a CSV template mirroring the operations travel itinerary; JSON remains the lossless internal format. Events support fixed or movable timing, explicit durations, location, and kickoff-relative or absolute anchoring. Protected sleep windows are rule-proposed per night, can be overridden by staff, and remain visibly distinct from recorded sleep.
40	
41	The comparison reports opportunity for each night of the weekend (Thursday, Friday, Saturday) against one editable target, shortfall, changed events, conflicts, fixed events that differ from the baseline, and every assumption used. 42	
43	Excluded from Release 1: forecasting engines and effectiveness curves, subgroups and non-travel reporting, individual athlete profiles and sleep observations, a staff editing UI, the athlete mobile itinerary, generated alternatives, hosting and role-based access, injury probabilities, individual clearance decisions, invented effectiveness percentages, automatic medication advice, inferred sleep-stage quality, production wearable connectors, and claims of exact FAST compatibility. These exclusions define product scope rather than a permanent limit on later work.

48	|---|---|
49	| Scenario | ID; title; parent revision; horizon (Thursday evening–Sunday midday); game type (road or home-with-hotel); kickoff instant and IANA zone; kickoff band; display zone; event revision; assumption-set ID |
50	| KickoffBandTemplate | Band (early, afternoon, night); game type; per entry and night marker, either offsets from kickoff or a clock time (day from game day + local time) for Friday practice start/end, Friday meetings start/end, curfew, wake-up call, meals, and departure to the stadium; source and revision |
51	| Event | ID; kind; title; anchoring (absolute, or offset from kickoff); start/end UTC instants; original local times and IANA zones; fixed or movable; allowed start window; minimum duration; location; source |
52	| ProtectedSleepWindow | Night; interval; opportunity type such as hotel/home/flight/nap; rule-proposed or staff-overridden; which edge each bound came from; assumptions; incompatible obligations |
53	| AssumptionSet | Sleep target; wind-down buffer (`pre_bed_minutes`, the same value `evaluate()` applies after every obligation; fixtures use 30 minutes pending staff confirmation); Saturday assumed wake time (`saturday_night_wake`); morning transition (`morning_minutes`); source; creation time (not yet recorded) |
54	| ModelRun | Input hash/revision; adapter name/version; parameters; initialization; requested/supported outputs; warnings; generated time; result units |
55	| Comparison | Baseline/candidate revisions; common assumptions; per-night interval definitions; differences; fixed-event changes; feasibility; model-run references |
56	
57	Kickoff bands: **early** kicks off before 12:00, **afternoon** 12:00–17:59, **night** 18:00 or later, all in the game's local zone. Band selection follows from the kickoff time; any template offset may then be edited in the scenario. A movable offset is a lever; kickoff is not.
58

When they return: do not duplicate person identifiers into public exports, evaluate group membership at the scenario revision, and never let a change in a person's group silently alter an older result.

# STATUS

Read this first. Update it before ending every session.

## Current state

Release 1 design confirmed 2026-09-15 (decisions table in
`SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md`). Package 1 (calendar core) and Package 1b
(game-weekend model) are implemented test-first on branch
`worktree-calendar-core`, draft PR #1. 163 tests pass; run `python -m pytest`
from the repo root. Records: `docs/handoffs/2026-09-15-game-weekend-model.md`
(model build, itinerary review).

**2026-09-16: the model was reshaped for the real itineraries.** The six
itinerary questions were adopted at their recommended answers and **confirmed
by the user the same day**; see the table under "Decisions from the first real
itineraries" in the spec's "Protected sleep window rule" section. Built
test-first:

- **Clock-time anchoring.** `weekend.ClockTime(day, "HH:MM")` (day counted from
  game day, `-1` = Friday) can place a template entry's edges or a night's
  curfew/wake instead of a kickoff offset. An entry uses one anchoring for both
  edges. Clock entries carry no `KickoffAnchor`, so a kickoff change moves
  Saturday and reports nothing for Friday. Offset overrides must match the
  entry's anchoring.
- **Window start rule (closes old open question 7).** Only an obligation that
  begins before the current start pushes it. Later ones stay inside the window
  as reported conflicts. A breakfast window opening before the wake-up call now
  clips the night instead of erasing it.
- **Nights without a curfew.** `NightMarker(curfew=None, released_by=<event id>)`
  starts at that event's end + `AssumptionSet.release_to_bed_minutes`
  (source `release:<id>`). The CLI prints and labels that assumption.
- **File format.** Optional keys `<edge>_clock`, `released_by`,
  `release_to_bed_minutes`; `FORMAT_VERSION` still 1, old fixtures load
  unchanged, and the CLI example output is unchanged.

Checked in memory against the real Auburn times (nothing saved): Friday with
breakfast as check-in 21:30 → 08:45 ET, 11h15m, set by curfew, which matches the
Drive review. As a whole breakfast block it is 10h00m with a visible conflict,
where it was 0h before. Saturday: bus arrival 23:15 CT + 45m → 00:00, 9h to the
assumed 09:00 wake.

The first two real staff itineraries (Auburn, PVAMU) live on Drive, not in Git:
`G:\My Drive\00_Primary_Storage_Drive\99_UNSORTED\From_Desktop\TECHNOLOGY\FAST\GAME_WEEK_ITINERARIES\2026\`,
with extracted times and offsets in `extracted-timeline-review.md` there.

Working example — the Friday early-kickoff comparison:

```bash
PYTHONPATH=src python -m sleep_scheduler \
  fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-baseline.json fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-candidate.json
```

An early road kickoff: 11:00 MT Saturday, home in Central time. In the baseline
Friday meetings run 22:00–23:00 MT, so with a 30-minute wind-down the Friday
window starts at 23:30 instead of the 23:00 curfew: 6h30m. Moving meetings an
hour earlier lets curfew set the start: 7h00m, +30m. Thursday (8h) and Saturday
(10h, to an assumed 09:00 wake) are unchanged, and only a movable event changed,
so there are no flags. Every offset, curfew, and wake time is synthetic. This
fixture still uses offset anchoring and a Saturday curfew; the synthetic
`home_night_template()` in `tests/synthetic.py` shows the itinerary-shaped form
(clock Friday, breakfast check-in, released Saturday).

| Module | What it does |
|---|---|
| `temporal.py` | Local wall time + IANA zone → UTC instant; half-open intervals; merge/subtract |

| `opportunity.py` | Spec steps 1–8; conflicts; comparison with changed, removed, added, and fixed-event changes |
| `weekend.py` | Kickoff bands, `ClockTime`, templates, `build_weekend`, the sleep window rule, `evaluate_weekend` / `compare_weekends`, flags |
| `adapter.py` | Forecast seam; the only adapter returns a status, never a number |
| `persistence.py` | Scenario JSON round-trip; game-weekend files (inputs only, rebuilt on load) |
| `cli.py` | `python -m sleep_scheduler <baseline weekend> <candidate weekend>` |

## Design confirmed (2026-09-15)

The full answer table is in `SLEEP-SCHEDULER-SPEC.md` under "Release 1 design
decisions". In short: Release 1 compares Baylor football game weekends
(Thursday evening to Sunday midday) for **Friday practice/meeting times against
Saturday kickoff** and **road-game departures, including the late return**. It
reports sleep opportunity per night for one group (the travel party, or the
whole roster at home). Applied Performance runs it locally: CSV in, one-page
HTML comparison out. There is no Sunday lift (player off day), and subgroups
are out of Release 1.

## Next

1. **Staff confirm the six working assumptions** (spec table) and **verify the
   extracted itinerary times** in the Drive review file. Both are human steps.
   If an answer differs, the model already supports the alternative except
   decision 1–2 "no" (kickoff-anchored Friday), which is just offset entries.
2. **Draft real templates on Drive** (afternoon band from Auburn, night band
   from PVAMU) once times are verified: clock-time Friday, kickoff Saturday,
   breakfast as check-in, "available" items optional, Saturday
   `released_by` the bus/game, no Thursday marker, neutral site as road. Load
   from Drive; never commit.
3. **Package 2:** CSV template shaped like the staff itinerary (time, item,
   location, duration, zone marker on travel legs). It must express both
   anchorings and `released_by`.
4. **Package 3:** printable one-page HTML comparison; the CLI report is its
   content model.

- Deferred out of Release 1: forecast engine, subgroups/non-travel,
  `SleepObservation`, candidate generation (CP-SAT), archive migration, the
  athlete mobile itinerary, hosting and roles.
- `AGENTS.md` still carries an unfolded `.from-windows` merge block (a stale
  pre-interview copy); safe to delete once someone confirms nothing in it is
  wanted.

## Open questions

1. The six itinerary assumptions above: confirmation pending (staff).
2. A home game with a Friday hotel uses `at="away"` (game zone = home zone) to
   mark the Friday window as a hotel window. Fine for now; revisit if a
   template needs a hotel in the home zone on a road trip.
3. Should the first obligation after the start ever push it (a travel leg
   departing after curfew)? Under a curfew it is now a conflict. Real itineraries
   put no travel after curfew, and Saturday uses release instead. Revisit only
   if a real case appears.
4. **Released nights have no floor.** `released_by` assumes a late release. For
   an early home kickoff (game over ~15:00, +45m) the window line would print a
   mid-afternoon start while the table clips it to the 18:00 reporting start
   (~15h). Options: allow `curfew` and `released_by` together (start = the later
   of the two), or give the early band a clock-time Saturday curfew. Decide when
   an early-kickoff itinerary arrives; do not draft an early template before.

Still needed from staff: verification of the extracted itinerary times, an
early-kickoff itinerary, and confirmation of the 30-minute wind-down buffer.

## Gotchas

- **Real itineraries never go in Git.** They are team schedules (AGENTS.md
  archive boundary). Keep them and anything derived from them on Drive. The
  synthetic home template copies their *shape*, never their times.
- `zoneinfo` does not refuse impossible local times; `temporal.LocalTime`
  raises on DST gaps and ambiguous times. Do not bypass it. `ClockTime`
  resolves through it.
- `Interval` equality ignores zone provenance on purpose; round-trip tests
  compare serialized dicts to check zones.
- Events are mandatory **by default**; only `schedule.OPTIONAL_KINDS` are
  ignored. Never reintroduce a mandatory whitelist. "Treatment available"-style
  items must be entered with an optional kind.
- Curfew and wake-up are `NightMarker`s, never Events. A marker has exactly one
  of `curfew` or `released_by`.
- The wind-down buffer **is** `pre_bed_minutes`; do not add a second field.
  `release_to_bed_minutes` is different: it *replaces* the buffer at a
  released night's start.
- `morning_minutes` widens the block before every obligation and can clip the
  window before a wake-up call; fixtures use 0.
- A staff end override is settled before obligations are checked; a start
  override is applied after.
- Night reporting intervals are fixed by date (18:00–12:00 in the night's zone,
  dated from the start before any push). Never derive them from the proposed
  window.
- Kickoff-anchored events compare by offset; a kickoff change is one
  `kickoff_shift`. Clock events compare by instant. Change detection covers
  start, end, removed, and added.
- `ClockTime.day` counts from the kickoff date **on the stadium clock**.
- Game-weekend files store inputs and are rebuilt on load; never add resolved
  instants. Newer keys are optional, so `FORMAT_VERSION` is 1.
- The CLI reads game-weekend files only; `--window` is gone.
- Itinerary "EST/CST" in September means daylight time; use IANA zones.
- The synthetic fixtures were generated once from `tests/synthetic.py`; the
  generator was not kept. Edit the JSON directly.

## Staff CSV format (Package 2, 2026-09-16)

One CSV holds one week's itinerary and becomes one game weekend (the same inputs a game-weekend JSON file stores). The CLI accepts `.csv` or `.json` for either side of a comparison. Staff never type IANA zones in rows and never edit JSON.

**Settings block.** The file opens with a `setting,value` header row and one setting per row, then a blank row, then the itinerary table.

| Setting | Required | Meaning |
|---|---|---|
| `id`, `title` | yes | Scenario id and report title |
| `kickoff` | yes | `YYYY-MM-DD HH:MM`, local to `kickoff_at` |
| `kickoff_at` | no (`away`) | `home` or `away` |
| `home_zone`, `game_zone` | yes | IANA zones (a home game uses the same zone twice) |
| `game_type` | yes | `road` or `home`; neutral site is `road` |
| `source` | yes | Where the times came from |
| `sleep_target_hours`, `pre_bed_minutes`, `morning_minutes`, `assumptions_source` | yes | The assumption set |
| `saturday_night_wake`, `release_to_bed_minutes` | no | Assumed wake time; release-to-bed time for a night without a curfew |

**Itinerary table.** Header `kind,day,start,end,title,at,arrive_at,movable,releases,id`, one row per item.

- `kind`: `practice`, `meeting`, `walkthrough`, `meal`, `travel`, `game`, `treatment`, `lift`, `class`, `media`, `other` (obligations); `optional`, `free`, `unstructured` (ignored, e.g. "treatment available"); `curfew`, `wake-up` (night markers, never events). Any other kind is refused: the model treats unknown kinds as obligations, so a typo would silently block sleep.
- `day`: `Thu`, `Fri`, `Sat`, `Sun` (full names accepted), counted around the kickoff date on the stadium clock.
- `start`, `end`: a clock time `HH:MM` on `day`, or a kickoff offset `K-4:15` / `K+3:45` / `K` (no `day` needed). An `end` clock time earlier than `start` is the next day. An obligation needs an end after its start; enter a breakfast as its check-in with a 5–10 minute duration. Curfew and wake-up rows have no end.
- **Anchoring follows the confirmed decisions, with no column for it.** Kickoff offsets are kickoff-anchored. A clock time before game day stays a clock time (Friday). A clock time on game day or later is converted to an offset from this file's kickoff (Saturday follows kickoff).
- `at`, `arrive_at`: `home` or `away` (default `home`); `arrive_at` only on travel legs that change zone.
- `movable`: `yes`/`no`; blank means yes for `practice`, `meeting`, `travel` (the Q7 levers) and no otherwise.
- `releases`: `yes` on the obligation whose end starts a night with no curfew (the bus back to the facility; the game at home).
- `id`: optional; blank becomes `<day>-<title>`. Ids tie a candidate's rows to the baseline's, so keep them when editing a copy; duplicates are refused.

**Nights.** A curfew row bounds the night of its evening; a wake-up row ends the night before it; a `releases` row starts the night its end falls in. Nights are named `thu`/`fri`/`sat` and ordered by date. Refused: a night with a wake-up but no curfew or release, a night with both, or a curfew and wake-up in different places. No Thursday rows means no Thursday night.

**Import validation** reports every bad row at once, by row number.

**Export** writes a weekend back to this format: clock rows before game day, kickoff offsets on game day and after, every `id` and `movable` filled in. A weekend with staff window overrides or extra clock events is refused rather than exported lossily. Round trip: events, anchoring, and zones unchanged.

**Comparing kickoff slots.** Export (or write) Saturday rows as `K` offsets and change `kickoff` in the copy: the Saturday rows re-flow and Friday stays put. Retyping Saturday clock times against a new kickoff describes a different schedule, and every Saturday row is then reported as moved.

**Real itineraries** filled into this format stay on Drive. The repo ignores `itineraries/` so a working copy cannot be committed by accident; fixtures are synthetic.

"""The staff CSV format: an itinerary-shaped file in, a game weekend out.

Spec: "Staff CSV format (Package 2)". The fixture pair in ``fixtures/`` is the
synthetic home-with-hotel weekend from ``tests/synthetic.py``, written the way
staff would type an itinerary: Friday and Saturday both as clock times.
"""

from dataclasses import replace
from pathlib import Path

import pytest

from sleep_scheduler.cli import main
from sleep_scheduler.itinerary_csv import (
    CsvFormatError,
    load_weekend_csv,
    weekend_from_csv,
    weekend_to_csv,
)
from sleep_scheduler.persistence import scenario_to_dict
from sleep_scheduler.schedule import Event, KickoffAnchor
from sleep_scheduler.temporal import Interval, LocalTime
from sleep_scheduler.weekend import ClockTime, WindowOverride, build_weekend, compare_weekends
from synthetic import (
    ASSUMPTIONS,
    CHICAGO,
    DENVER,
    EARLY_KICKOFF,
    FRIDAY,
    H,
    HOME_ASSUMPTIONS,
    HOME_KICKOFF,
    M,
    home_night_template,
    road_early_released_template,
)

FIXTURES = Path(__file__).resolve().parents[1] / "fixtures"
BASELINE = FIXTURES / "home-night-hotel-baseline.csv"
CANDIDATE = FIXTURES / "home-night-hotel-candidate.csv"

SETTINGS = """setting,value
id,x
title,X (synthetic)
kickoff,2026-10-10 19:00
home_zone,America/Chicago
game_zone,America/Chicago
game_type,home
source,synthetic
sleep_target_hours,8
pre_bed_minutes,30
morning_minutes,0
assumptions_source,synthetic
saturday_night_wake,09:00
release_to_bed_minutes,60
"""
HEADER = "kind,day,start,end,title,at,arrive_at,movable,releases,id\n"
NIGHTS = """curfew,Fri,22:00,,Curfew,away,,,,
wake-up,Sat,10:00,,Wake-up,away,,,,
game,Sat,19:00,23:00,Game,home,,,yes,game
"""


def csv(rows="", nights=NIGHTS, settings=SETTINGS):
    return settings + "\n" + HEADER + rows + nights


def events(weekend):
    return {e.id: e for e in weekend.scenario.events}


def home_weekend():
    return build_weekend(
        home_night_template(),
        HOME_KICKOFF,
        home_zone=CHICAGO,
        game_zone=CHICAGO,
        assumptions=HOME_ASSUMPTIONS,
        id="home-night-baseline",
        title="Home night kickoff (synthetic)",
    )


# --- The fixture expresses the tested model exactly ---------------------------------


def test_itinerary_csv_imports_to_the_synthetic_home_weekend():
    weekend = load_weekend_csv(BASELINE)
    expected = home_weekend()
    assert weekend.template == expected.template
    assert weekend.scenario.assumptions == HOME_ASSUMPTIONS
    assert scenario_to_dict(weekend.scenario) == scenario_to_dict(expected.scenario)


def test_candidate_csv_moves_only_the_meetings_and_costs_friday_fifteen_minutes():
    comparison = compare_weekends(load_weekend_csv(BASELINE), load_weekend_csv(CANDIDATE))
    assert [c.event_id for c in comparison.changed_events] == ["fri-meeting"]
    assert comparison.flags == []
    assert comparison.night("fri").hours_delta == -0.25
    assert comparison.night("sat").hours_delta == 0.0


def test_cli_compares_two_csv_files(capsys):
    assert main([str(BASELINE), str(CANDIDATE)]) == 0
    out = capsys.readouterr().out
    assert "sleep opportunity" in out.lower()
    assert "fri-meeting" in out


# --- Anchoring ---------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_friday_clock_row_stays_on_the_clock():
    meeting = weekend_from_csv(csv("meeting,Fri,20:00,21:00,Meetings,home,,,,fri-meeting\n"))
    template_entry = next(e for e in meeting.template.entries if e.id == "fri-meeting")
    assert (template_entry.start, template_entry.end) == (ClockTime(FRIDAY, "20:00"), ClockTime(FRIDAY, "21:00"))
    assert events(meeting)["fri-meeting"].anchor is None


def test_game_day_clock_row_becomes_an_offset_from_this_files_kickoff():
    weekend = weekend_from_csv(csv("meal,Sat,15:40,16:10,Pregame meal,home,,,,sat-meal\n"))
    assert events(weekend)["sat-meal"].anchor == KickoffAnchor(-3 * H - 20 * M, -2 * H - 50 * M, CHICAGO, CHICAGO)


def test_kickoff_offset_rows_re_flow_when_the_kickoff_setting_changes():
    rows = "meal,,K-3:30,K-3:00,Pregame meal,home,,,,sat-meal\nmeeting,Fri,20:00,21:00,Meetings,home,,,,fri-meeting\n"
    early = events(weekend_from_csv(csv(rows)))
    later = events(weekend_from_csv(csv(rows, settings=SETTINGS.replace("19:00", "20:00"))))
    assert later["sat-meal"].interval.start - early["sat-meal"].interval.start == H
    assert later["fri-meeting"].interval == early["fri-meeting"].interval


def test_clock_end_before_start_is_the_next_day():
    weekend = weekend_from_csv(csv("meeting,Fri,23:30,00:30,Late film,home,,,,film\n"))
    film = events(weekend)["film"]
    assert (film.interval.wall("start"), film.interval.wall("end")) == ("2026-10-09T23:30", "2026-10-10T00:30")


def test_travel_leg_departs_home_and_arrives_away():
    settings = SETTINGS.replace("game_zone,America/Chicago", "game_zone,America/Denver").replace(
        "kickoff,2026-10-10 19:00", "kickoff,2026-10-10 18:00"
    )
    nights = "curfew,Fri,22:00,,Curfew,away,,,,\nwake-up,Sat,09:00,,Wake,away,,,,\n"
    rows = "travel,Fri,12:00,13:00,Charter,home,away,,,fri-depart\n"
    flight = events(weekend_from_csv(csv(rows, nights=nights, settings=settings)))["fri-depart"]
    assert (flight.interval.start_zone, flight.interval.end_zone) == (CHICAGO, DENVER)
    assert (flight.interval.wall("start"), flight.interval.wall("end")) == ("2026-10-09T12:00", "2026-10-09T12:00")


# --- Nights ------------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_curfew_wake_up_and_release_rows_become_night_markers_not_events():
    weekend = weekend_from_csv(csv())
    assert [m.night for m in weekend.template.nights] == ["fri", "sat"]
    fri, sat = weekend.template.nights
    assert (fri.curfew, fri.wake, fri.at) == (ClockTime(FRIDAY, "22:00"), -9 * H, "away")
    assert (sat.curfew, sat.wake, sat.released_by) == (None, None, "game")
    assert set(events(weekend)) == {"game"}


def test_no_thursday_rows_means_no_thursday_night():
    assert "thu" not in [m.night for m in weekend_from_csv(csv()).template.nights]


def test_wake_up_without_a_curfew_or_release_is_refused():
    nights = "wake-up,Sat,10:00,,Wake-up,away,,,,\ngame,Sat,19:00,23:00,Game,home,,,,game\n"
    with pytest.raises(CsvFormatError, match="fri night"):
        weekend_from_csv(csv(nights=nights))


def test_night_with_both_a_curfew_and_a_release_is_refused():
    nights = NIGHTS + "curfew,Sat,23:30,,Curfew,home,,,,\n"
    with pytest.raises(CsvFormatError, match="sat night"):
        weekend_from_csv(csv(nights=nights))


# --- Validation --------------------------------------------------------------------


def test_unknown_kind_is_refused_with_its_row_and_the_allowed_kinds():
    with pytest.raises(CsvFormatError, match=r"row 17.*optinal.*optional"):
        weekend_from_csv(csv("optinal,Fri,21:00,22:00,Treatment available,home,,,,t\n"))


def test_zero_duration_obligation_is_refused_with_the_check_in_hint():
    with pytest.raises(CsvFormatError, match="check-in"):
        weekend_from_csv(csv("meal,Sat,10:30,10:30,Breakfast check-in,home,,,,b\n"))


def test_every_bad_row_is_reported_at_once():
    rows = "optinal,Fri,21:00,22:00,T,home,,,,t\nmeal,Sat,25:00,26:00,Breakfast,home,,,,b\n"
    with pytest.raises(CsvFormatError) as caught:
        weekend_from_csv(csv(rows))

"""Compare two game-weekend files and print sleep opportunity night by night.

Usage::

    python -m sleep_scheduler fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-baseline.json \\
                              fixtures/friday-early-kickoff-candidate.json

The wording here is deliberately constrained. The report says "opportunity",
names the source of its target, labels every assumption as one, says what set
each edge of each sleep window, and prints the forecast status rather than a
forecast. It has no vocabulary for effectiveness, fatigue, or readiness,
because nothing in this codebase can compute them.
"""

from __future__ import annotations

import argparse
import sys
from datetime import timedelta
from pathlib import Path
from zoneinfo import ZoneInfo

from .adapter import get_adapter
from .persistence import load_weekend
from .weekend import NightReport, WeekendComparison, compare_weekends

__all__ = ["main", "render_weekend_comparison"]


def _hhmm(hours: float) -> str:
    total = round(abs(hours) * 60)
    return f"{total // 60}h {total % 60:02d}m"


def _signed_hhmm(hours: float) -> str:
    return ("+" if hours >= 0 else "-") + _hhmm(hours)


def _shift(delta: timedelta) -> str:
    minutes = round(delta.total_seconds() / 60)
    if minutes == 0:
        return "unchanged"
    direction = "later" if minutes > 0 else "earlier"
    return f"{abs(minutes) // 60}h {abs(minutes) % 60:02d}m {direction}"


def _window_line(label: str, night: NightReport) -> str:
    name = night.night.capitalize()
    window = night.plan.window
    if window is None:
        return f"  {label} {name}: no window ({night.note})"
    zone = ZoneInfo(window.interval.start_zone)
    start = window.interval.start.astimezone(zone).strftime("%a %H:%M")
    end = window.interval.end.astimezone(zone).strftime("%a %H:%M")
    return (
        f"  {label} {name}: {start} -> {end} {window.interval.start_zone} "
        f"(start: {window.start_source}; end: {window.end_source})"
    )


def render_weekend_comparison(comparison: WeekendComparison) -> str:
    baseline, candidate = comparison.baseline, comparison.candidate
    weekend = candidate.weekend
    assumptions = weekend.scenario.assumptions
    lines: list[str] = []

    lines.append("Measure: sleep opportunity (not sleep obtained), reported per night")
    lines.append(f"Baseline:  {baseline.weekend.scenario.title}")
    lines.append(f"Candidate: {weekend.scenario.title}")
    kickoff = weekend.kickoff.astimezone(ZoneInfo(weekend.game_zone))
    lines.append(
        f"Kickoff: {kickoff:%a %Y-%m-%d %H:%M} {weekend.game_zone} "
        f"({weekend.template.band} band); home zone {weekend.home_zone}"
    )
    lines.append(f"Template: {weekend.template.source}")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append(f"{'Night':<6}{'Baseline':>10}{'Candidate':>11}{'Difference':>12}")
    for name, night in comparison.nights:
        lines.append(
            f"{name.capitalize():<6}{_hhmm(night.baseline.hours):>10}"
            f"{_hhmm(night.candidate.hours):>11}{_signed_hhmm(night.hours_delta):>12}"
        )
    shortfalls = ", ".join(
        f"{name.capitalize()} {_hhmm(night.candidate.shortfall_hours)}"
        for name, night in comparison.nights
    )
    lines.append(f"Candidate shortfall against target: {shortfalls}")
    lines.append("")

    lines.append("Protected sleep windows (what set each edge):")
    for label, report in (("Baseline", baseline), ("Candidate", candidate)):
        for night in report.nights:
            lines.append(_window_line(label, night))
    lines.append("")

    lines.append(f"Target: {_hhmm(assumptions.sleep_target_hours)} (source: {assumptions.source})")
    lines.append(
        f"Assumptions: wind-down buffer of {assumptions.pre_bed_minutes} min after the last "
        f"obligation; {assumptions.morning_minutes} min before a morning obligation"
    )
    if assumptions.saturday_night_wake:
        lines.append(
            f"Saturday night ends at an assumed wake time of {assumptions.saturday_night_wake} "
            "(an assumption, not an obligation: Sunday is a player off day)"
        )
    if assumptions.release_to_bed_minutes is not None:
        lines.append(
            f"A night without a curfew starts an assumed {assumptions.release_to_bed_minutes} min "
            "after its releasing obligation ends (release to in bed; an assumption, "
            "not a schedule time)"
        )
    lines.append("")

    if comparison.changed_events:
        lines.append("Changed events:")
        for change in comparison.changed_events:
            lines.append(
                f"  - {change.event_id}: start {_shift(change.shift)}, end {_shift(change.end_shift)}"
            )
    else:
        lines.append("Changed events: none")
    if comparison.added_events:
        lines.append(f"Added in candidate: {', '.join(comparison.added_events)}")

    if comparison.flags:
        lines.append("Flags:")
        for flag in comparison.flags:
            lines.append(f"  ! {flag}")
    else:
        lines.append("Flags: none (only movable events changed)")
    lines.append("")

    conflicts = [
        (label, night.night, conflict)
        for label, report in (("Baseline", baseline), ("Candidate", candidate))
        for night in report.nights
        for conflict in night.report.conflicts
    ]
    if conflicts:
        lines.append("Conflicts (not resolved automatically):")
        for label, name, conflict in conflicts:
            lines.append(f"  - {label} {name.capitalize()}: {conflict.describe()}")
    else:
        lines.append("Conflicts: none")
    lines.append("")

    adapter = get_adapter()
    first_night = candidate.nights[0].report
    result = adapter.simulate(first_night, requires_travel=weekend.home_zone != weekend.game_zone)
    lines.append(f"Forecast ({result.adapter_name} v{result.adapter_version}): {result.reason}")
    warnings: list[str] = []
    for night in candidate.nights:
        for warning in adapter.validate(night.report):
            if warning not in warnings:
                warnings.append(warning)
    for warning in warnings:
        lines.append(f"  ! {warning}")

    return "\n".join(lines)


def main(argv: list[str] | None = None) -> int:
    parser = argparse.ArgumentParser(
        prog="sleep_scheduler",
        description="Compare sleep opportunity night by night between two game-weekend files.",
    )
    parser.add_argument("baseline", type=Path)
    parser.add_argument("candidate", type=Path)
    args = parser.parse_args(argv)

    try:
        comparison = compare_weekends(load_weekend(args.baseline), load_weekend(args.candidate))
    except FileNotFoundError as exc:
        print(f"error: cannot read {exc.filename}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2
    except (ValueError, KeyError) as exc:
        print(f"error: {exc}", file=sys.stderr)
        return 2

    print(render_weekend_comparison(comparison))
    return 0


if __name__ == "__main__":
    raise SystemExit(main())

attachment.snippet:
1	# Sleep Scheduler Implementation Specification
2	
3	Status: Release 1 design confirmed with the user on September 15, 2026, through the design interview recorded below. The calendar core, opportunity calculation, and the game-weekend model (Package 1b) are implemented on branch `worktree-calendar-core` (see `docs/STATUS.md`); CSV input (Package 2) is implemented (see "Staff CSV format"); the HTML comparison (Package 3) is specified, not yet built. Research basis: [FAST modernization research](FAST-MODERNIZATION-RESEARCH.md). No physiological model has been implemented or validated.
4	
5	## Product objective
6	
7	Help Applied Performance compare feasible Baylor football game-weekend schedules that protect sleep opportunities around practice, meetings, travel, and competition. Provide a reproducible explanation of each difference. Add fatigue predictions through an explicitly identified model only after its capabilities and evidence have been evaluated.
8	
9	The decisions Release 1 supports are:
10	
11	- **Friday practice and meeting times** relative to Saturday's kickoff.
12	- **Departure times** for road games, outbound and post-game (the late return).
13	
14	The first complete workflow is a Friday comparison before an early road kickoff: build a baseline game weekend from a kickoff-band template; duplicate it; move Friday practice or meeting times; compare per-night opportunity and conflicts; export a one-page comparison. Use synthetic data for development. Historical football schedules become fixtures only after staff verifies their interpretation.
15	
16	## Release 1 design decisions (interview, 2026-09-15)
17	
18	| # | Decision | Settled answer |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| Q1/Q16 | Decision the app improves | Friday practice/meeting timing against Saturday kickoff, and road-game departures including the late return. First working example: Friday times before an early road kickoff. |
21	| Q2 | Forecasting | Sleep opportunity only. An engine is expected later; not a FAST replacement until then. |
22	| Q3/Q12/Q19 | Who is modelled | One group per scenario: the travel party (road) or the full roster (home). No subgroups, no individual athlete data, no non-travel reporting in Release 1. |
23	| Q4 | Operation | Applied Performance creates and interprets; coaches and operations review the one-page comparison and decide. Athletes are not users. |
24	| Q5 | Scenario unit | One game weekend, Thursday evening through Sunday midday. Road games and home games with a Friday team hotel. Neutral-site games are road games (confirmed 2026-09-16). |
25	| Q6 | Kickoff anchoring | Game-related events are stored as offsets from kickoff; changing kickoff re-flows them. Comparing kickoff slots = duplicate and change kickoff. Amended 2026-09-16: Friday curfew, practice, and meetings are clock times chosen per week; kickoff drives Saturday. |
26	| Q7 | Movable levers | Departures, Friday practice, and meeting times. Kickoff is fixed. |
27	| Q10 | Sunday | Player off day. No lift on Sunday (lifts are Monday and Wednesday). |
28	| Q11 | Sleep window rule | Rule-proposed per night from explicit practice times, practice lead time before kickoff, curfew, and meeting times (see "Protected sleep window rule"). |
29	| Q13/Q18 | Templates | Same timeline shape each week, timing varies with kickoff: three kickoff-band templates. |
30	| Q14 | Target | One editable target for all nights. |
31	| Q17 | Saturday night | Ends at an editable assumed wake time, labelled as an assumption. |
32	| Q9 | Input and output | CSV template shaped like the operations itinerary in; printable one-page HTML comparison out. |
33	| Q15 | Deployment | Local on the Applied Performance laptop. No hosting, login, or roles. |
34	
35	Values still needed from staff (data, not decisions): real template offsets per band, the Saturday assumed wake time, and confirmation of the 30-minute wind-down default. Fixtures use visibly synthetic values until then.
36	
37	## Release 1 scope
38	
39	Input is a CSV template mirroring the operations travel itinerary; JSON remains the lossless internal format. Events support fixed or movable timing, explicit durations, location, and kickoff-relative or absolute anchoring. Protected sleep windows are rule-proposed per night, can be overridden by staff, and remain visibly distinct from recorded sleep.
40	
41	The comparison reports opportunity for each night of the weekend (Thursday, Friday, Saturday) against one editable target, shortfall, changed events, conflicts, fixed events that differ from the baseline, and every assumption used. A local/home-time switch must preserve event instants. Output is a printable one-page HTML file that can be saved as PDF. Exports are local files, not automatic messages or calendar publication.
42	
43	Excluded from Release 1: forecasting engines and effectiveness curves, subgroups and non-travel reporting, individual athlete profiles and sleep observations, a staff editing UI, the athlete mobile itinerary, generated alternatives, hosting and role-based access, injury probabilities, individual clearance decisions, invented effectiveness percentages, automatic medication advice, inferred sleep-stage quality, production wearable connectors, and claims of exact FAST compatibility. These exclusions define product scope rather than a permanent limit on later work.
44	
45	## Domain contract
46	
47	| Object | Required fields and semantics |
48	|---|---|
49	| Scenario | ID; title; parent revision; horizon (Thursday evening–Sunday midday); game type (road or home-with-hotel); kickoff instant and IANA zone; kickoff band; display zone; event revision; assumption-set ID |
50	| KickoffBandTemplate | Band (early, afternoon, night); game type; per entry and night marker, either offsets from kickoff or a clock time (day from game day + local time) for Friday practice start/end, Friday meetings start/end, curfew, wake-up call, meals, and departure to the stadium; source and revision |
51	| Event | ID; kind; title; anchoring (absolute, or offset from kickoff); start/end UTC instants; original local times and IANA zones; fixed or movable; allowed start window; minimum duration; location; source |
52	| ProtectedSleepWindow | Night; interval; opportunity type such as hotel/home/flight/nap; rule-proposed or staff-overridden; which edge each bound came from; assumptions; incompatible obligations |
53	| AssumptionSet | Sleep target; wind-down buffer (`pre_bed_minutes`, the same value `evaluate()` applies after every obligation; fixtures use 30 minutes pending staff confirmation); Saturday assumed wake time (`saturday_night_wake`); morning transition (`morning_minutes`); source; creation time (not yet recorded) |
54	| ModelRun | Input hash/revision; adapter name/version; parameters; initialization; requested/supported outputs; warnings; generated time; result units |
55	| Comparison | Baseline/candidate revisions; common assumptions; per-night interval definitions; differences; fixed-event changes; feasibility; model-run references |
56	
57	Kickoff bands: **early** kicks off before 12:00, **afternoon** 12:00–17:59, **night** 18:00 or later, all in the game's local zone. Band selection follows from the kickoff time; any template offset may then be edited in the scenario. A movable offset is a lever; kickoff is not.
58	
59	Deferred with subgroups and individual modelling (not Release 1): `AthleteProfile` (pseudonymous ID; group membership; home IANA zone; optional sleep target and source; individual availability; optional habitual sleep timing and provenance), scenario group IDs, and `SleepObservation` (episode interval; source category; optional device/version; quality flags; revision; original record reference; observed versus imputed status). When they return: do not duplicate person identifiers into public exports, evaluate group membership at the scenario revision, and never let a change in a person's group silently alter an older result.
60	
61	## Temporal rules

7	Help Applied Performance compare feasible Baylor football game-weekend schedules that protect sleep opportunities around practice, meetings, travel, and competition. Provide a reproducible explanation of each difference. Add fatigue predictions through an explicitly identified model only after its capabilities and evidence have been evaluated.

9	The decisions Release 1 supports are:

11	- **Friday practice and meeting times** relative to Saturday's kickoff.
12	- **Departure times** for road games, outbound and post-game (the late return).
13

Use synthetic data for development. Historical football schedules become fixtures only after staff verifies their interpretation.
15	
16	## Release 1 design decisions (interview, 2026-09-15)
17	
18	| # | Decision | Settled answer |
19	|---|---|---|
20	| Q1/Q16 | Decision the app improves | Friday practice/meeting timing against Saturday kickoff, and road-game departures including the late return. First working example: Friday times before an early road kickoff. |
21	| Q2 | Forecasting | Sleep opportunity only. An engine is expected later; not a FAST replacement until then. |
22	| Q3/Q12/Q19 | Who is modelled | One group per scenario: the travel party (road) or the full roster (home). No subgroups, no individual athlete data, no non-travel reporting in Release 1. |
23	| Q4 | Operation | Applied Performance creates and interprets; coaches and operations review the one-page comparison and decide. Athletes are not users. |
24	| Q5 | Scenario unit | One game weekend, Thursday evening through Sunday midday. Road games and home games with a Friday team hotel. Neutral-site games are road games (confirmed 2026-09-16). |
25	| Q6 | Kickoff anchoring | Game-related events are stored as offsets from kickoff; changing kickoff re-flows them. Comparing kickoff slots = duplicate and change kickoff. Amended 2026-09-16: Friday curfew, practice, and meetings are clock times chosen per week; kickoff drives Saturday. |
26	| Q7 | Movable levers | Departures, Friday practice, and meeting times. Kickoff is fixed. |
27	| Q10 | Sunday | Player off day. No lift on Sunday (lifts are Monday and Wednesday). |
28	| Q11 | Sleep window rule | Rule-proposed per night from explicit practice times, practice lead time before kickoff, curfew, and meeting times (see "Protected sleep window rule"). |
29	| Q13/Q18 | Templates | Same timeline shape each week, timing varies with kickoff: three kickoff-band templates. |
30	| Q14 | Target | One editable target for all nights. |
31	| Q17 | Saturday night | Ends at an editable assumed wake time, labelled as an assumption. |

38	
39	Input is a CSV template mirroring the operations travel itinerary; JSON remains the lossless internal format. 40	
41	The comparison reports opportunity for each night of the weekend (Thursday, Friday, Saturday) against one editable target, shortfall, changed events, conflicts, fixed events that differ from the baseline, and every assumption used.
